correctness.rationale: Moraschini's Figure 1 and Theorem 5.1 identify the free algebra: 14 isotone two-valued evaluations of the seven modal terms give a 37-element upset lattice. The displayed Box and Diamond fixed points give the greatest fixed point below and least fixed point above each input, respectively, and match the primary diagram. Evaluating upset DNFs under each possible generator image gives all 37 candidate maps; an independent implementation checked constants, lattice operations and both modal operations on every candidate, and matched each map image to separate singleton closure. For ranks 2,4,5,6,8,10,12,13,16,17,22,23,29,37 it reproduced map counts 2,4,10,2,4,2,2,1,2,2,1,2,2,1 and idempotent counts 2,4,6,2,2,2,2,1,2,2,1,2,2,1. The four 5→4 and two 8→6 cases all satisfy e^3=e^2. Deduplicating the map images yields the displayed size distribution for 33 subalgebras; deduplicating idempotent images yields the displayed retract distribution for 27. Every retract corresponds to such an idempotent and the image of every endomorphism is generated by the image of x, so the counts are exhaustive. Replay: python3 /workspace/branches/f59464c1-b2c7-46a9-87fd-86cc9002e5c5/independent_enum.py (INDEPENDENT_ENUMERATION_OK).
residual_risks: This is exact finite verification of the stated free algebra, not a formal proof certificate or a theorem for additional generators.

value.rationale: The canonical free algebra is a natural object, and retracts of free algebras are relevant to projectivity in this setting. The exact image and idempotent spectra distinguish the endomorphisms from one another beyond the known total and unique surjection. Deduplication identifies which one-generated subalgebras can occur as retracts by size, and e^3=e^2 characterizes the stabilization of all exceptional maps. This is a useful finite classification, not a differently formatted recount of the elements of F.
residual_risks: No extension to higher-generated free algebras or full monoid classification is established.
